entries.title: Agents are written as a brief
entries.description: An agent's page now holds its purpose, goal, how to answer and never rules as one document: type @ to add a tool, a knowledge base or a skill, and the agent gets it. The test chat shows which step of a skill the agent is on, and a publish that cannot go ahead names the field that blocks it.

entries.title: Keep a look-up to one step of a skill
entries.description: A skill builder can now mark a step's tool as only for that step, so the agent cannot use it outside the skill even when it only reads.

entries.title: Skills can hold numbered steps
entries.description: A skill's page now has when to use it, notes and numbered steps in one place: type @ to name a tool, a knowledge base or another skill, and add a check to a step. A publish that cannot go ahead names the step that blocks it, and tests, versions, files and the agents that use the skill open from the page header instead of tabs.

entries.title: A skill's actions run only through its steps
entries.description: An agent can no longer use a skill's write action without the skill: the action is reached only at its step, and a check that fails ends the skill for that reply with the reason. A step that changes something needs a check written as a rule, and the publish check points at a step that names a tool without running it.

entries.title: Agent changes run one at a time
entries.description: When an agent makes several changes in one reply, they now run one after another instead of side by side, on every agent. A skill loaded in a chat now replaces the one loaded by the reply before, so skills no longer pile up as a conversation goes on.

entries.title: Agents that ask other agents share one budget
entries.description: When an agent asks another agent, both spend from the first conversation's budget, which is now checked before every model call: an agent asked at the cap stops and the first agent gives one closing answer. A scheduled run can ask the agents it was granted, and start workflows, in its own team only.

entries.title: Chats show where a skill is and how it ended
entries.description: Every chat now shows the step a skill is on and, under the reply it ended in, whether it finished, was blocked or stopped, with the reason. On a skill's page the tool you pick anywhere in a step becomes the tool that step runs, marked "runs".

entries.title: Reconnect notices name the environment
entries.description: The notice admins get when an app's team account stops working now says whether it is the sandbox or the production account.

entries.title: Refused events show in the team's Activity
entries.description: When an event does not match a workflow's inputs, the team's Activity and its account admins' Background page list a failed job saying which workflow did not run and which field was wrong.

entries.title: Reloading a skill keeps what you typed
entries.description: When someone else saves a skill before you, Reload now shows their version with your unsaved changes kept on top, ready to save. It used to drop them.

entries.title: Run inputs are checked against their declared types
entries.description: A workflow no longer starts with an input of the wrong type or a required field missing: the start is refused and names the field and the reason. A number typed as text, in a form, a spreadsheet or on the command line, is read as the number.

entries.title: Scheduled agent runs no longer ask other agents
entries.description: A run with no person behind it, such as a scheduled one, is not offered the agents it was granted, and its run log records which ones were withheld. Chats with a person work as before.
